newsitem.title: LEBANON: Israeli soldier, four guerrillas killed in Lebanon.
newsitem.headline: Israeli soldier, four guerrillas killed in Lebanon.

text.p: One Israeli soldier and four Hizbollah guerrillas were killed on Friday in the bloodiest clashes in south Lebanon in a month, Hizbollah and Israeli sources said.

The flareup on the last active Arab-Israeli frontline came two days after Israel's decision to build homes for Jews in Arab East Jerusalem -- a move that enraged many anti-Israeli Islamist and Palestinian guerrilla groups.
The Israeli death raised to five the number of Israeli soldiers killed in south Lebanon this year. Twenty-seven were killed last year.
Hizbollah guerrillas rained dozens of mortar bombs on army posts on the edge of Israel's south Lebanon occupation zone, sources in the pro-Israeli South Lebanon Army (SLA) said.
In Beirut, the pro-Iranian Hizbollah guerrilla group claimed responsibility for the attack and said four of its fighters were killed in the fighting.

In Israel the army said one soldier was killed and an officer was seriously wounded in the exchanges in the eastern sector of the south Lebanon security zone. It said two Hizbollah guerrillas were killed.
"Mortar and anti-tank fire were shot from early morning until the afternoon towards Israeli army and SLA forces. Hizbollah fired from various populated areas in the environs of Nabatiyeh.
"An Israeli army force returned fire and hit and killed two Hizbollah terrorists and it appears even more," the Israeli army said in a statement.

"The fighting was quite heavy. The Israelis fired about 200 shells in all. The guerrilla firing got heavy at times, three shells being fired (at the Israeli posts) every minute," one Lebanese security source told Reuters.

Hours later, Israeli planes raided suspected guerrilla targets north of the occupation zone. Witnesses said two jets fired two rockets into the Habboush river area but there was no word on casualties.
The Hizbollah attack was the third fatal one this year and the bloodiest since January 30 when three Israeli soldiers were killed and one wounded in a bomb attack.

The group, which is financed and armed by Tehran, linked its "new victory" against the Israelis with the fifth anniversary of the assassination of its chief Sheikh Abbas al-Musawi in an Israeli helicopter ambush in February 1992.
Hizbollah is fighting to oust 1,000 Israeli troops and 3,000 SLA militiamen from the 15-km (nine-miles)-deep south Lebanon zone set up to prevent raids on northern Israel.

On Thursday, Palestinian Islamist groups, which operate in the occupied territories, vowed in statements in Beirut to launch attacks against Israel in retaliation for its decision on Wednesday to build 6,500 homes for Jews in Arab East Jerusalem.
Syria, Lebanon's main power broker which wields considerable influence with Hizbollah, has criticised the Israeli decision, saying it meant Israel does not want peace.
